content.jointProblem: How can site-specific hydrogeological investigation and leachate transport modelling support a defensible four-well monitoring network and containment/treatment proposal for Zelena Petlja’s storage yard? The first investigation would test groundwater-flow and plume hypotheses using surveyed water levels and quality-controlled sampling, alongside bench tests of candidate treatment options on actual yard leachate, rather than assuming that published alluvial-aquifer designs or ammonium-removal results transfer to this COD-rich discharge.

rationale.text: Zorić has directly relevant consulting experience in groundwater monitoring design and assessment of interceptor drains at operating regional landfills.

sources.quote: groundwater monitoring programme design and interceptor drain performance assessment at two operational landfills in the Južna Bačka district.

rationale.text: Her research connects field monitoring of leachate indicators, including COD, with calibrated groundwater transport modelling.

sources.quote: Groundwater samples were collected quarterly and analysed for chloride, ammonium, COD, and electrical conductivity.
A calibrated MT3DMS transport model reproduced observed concentration profiles with a normalised root-mean-square error of 8.4 % for chloride and 14.1 % for ammonium.

rationale.text: Her transfer-station research addresses seasonal water-table changes and their implications for containment design, matching a key uncertainty at the yard.

sources.quote: Water table depths ranged from 0.4 m (spring snowmelt) to 3.1 m below ground (late summer)
Results indicate that containment designs based solely on mean annual conditions may underestimate peak infiltration by up to 40 % in this climatic setting.

rationale.text: She offers a field-tested basis for evaluating passive interceptor drains, while leaving their suitability at this site to investigation.

sources.quote: Chart validation was performed against three field installations in Vojvodina, where measured drain capture efficiencies ranged from 84 to 97 %

rationale.text: A joint project is explicitly compatible with her stated willingness to undertake site-specific leachate modelling and containment work.

sources.quote: contract research on site-specific leachate transport modelling and containment design

constraints.text: The work must address installation of four monitoring wells and a remediation submission under the inspectorate’s order. The stated late-June-2024 deadline must be checked before setting a current programme.

sources.quote: issued an order requiring us to install four groundwater monitoring wells within 120 days and to submit a remediation proposal.
all before the 120-day deadline runs out in late June 2024.

constraints.text: Well siting and model assumptions require updated site characterisation; neither plume extent nor seasonal groundwater-flow direction is established by the available historical sketch.

sources.quote: We have a hydrogeological sketch from when the site was first permitted in 1993 but nothing more recent.
We do not know how far the contamination has moved or which direction groundwater flows under the site at different seasons.

constraints.text: The proposal must address continuing leakage from the yard, not only monitor groundwater or treat an already established plume.

sources.quote: The liner under that area was never designed for liquid retention.
The leachate from our temporary storage yard has started seeping toward the site boundary

constraints.text: Treatment selection must address the reported COD burden and verify performance on the actual leachate; the supplied passive-barrier evidence concerns ammonium removal, not demonstrated COD treatment.

sources.quote: our last sampling showed COD at 3,400 mg/L
Permeable reactive barriers (PRBs) using natural zeolite (clinoptilolite) represent an inexpensive passive remediation option for ammonium-laden leachate plumes in alluvial aquifers.

constraints.text: External investigation, analytical capacity, drilling and implementation costs need an agreed funding route; the company has no dedicated research budget and only a basic laboratory.

sources.quote: we have no dedicated research budget or laboratory beyond the basic wet-chemistry bench used for leachate monitoring.

constraints.text: Researcher capacity must be confirmed for the actual project dates. The only dated availability indication concerns 2025/26 and cannot establish capacity for the stated 2024 deadline.

sources.quote: Zorić is on a reduced teaching load in the 2025/26 academic year due to project finalisation commitments

risks: The task deadline and researcher availability information refer to different periods. Current compliance status and actual availability are unknown, so timely delivery cannot be assumed.

Local stratigraphy, hydraulic connectivity and seasonal gradients may differ from the published alluvial sites. Initial water-level measurements, borehole logging and sampling must test transferability before adopting drain charts or transport parameters.

Published zeolite-column results address ammonium, and field-scale longevity was model-predicted. They do not establish COD removal or treatment durability for this yard; initial bench tests may rule out that option.
A four-well network and an initial sampling round may not resolve a complex plume or seasonal flow reversals. Additional investigation could be necessary beyond the minimum ordered network.
Funding, drilling access, external laboratory capacity and implementation contractors are unconfirmed; the company’s limited research resources could prevent execution.
The inspectorate’s detailed acceptance criteria and required professional sign-offs are unknown. Research outputs alone do not guarantee acceptance of the remediation proposal.
questions: What is the current status of the February order, the four wells and the late-June-2024 deadline? Can the full order, any extensions and regulator correspondence be shared?
Can Zorić confirm availability, field-team capacity and a delivery schedule for the actual project period?
What budget and procurement authority are available for drilling, surveying, independent laboratory analyses, modelling and containment works?
Can the company provide the 1993 sketch, permit documents, yard and utility plans, liner information, sampling records and analytical quality-control documentation?
What access is available on and beyond the eastern boundary, and are there nearby water abstractions or other sensitive groundwater receptors?
Which monitoring locations, well specifications, analytical parameters, treatment or discharge limits and professional approvals will the inspectorate require?
Can an initial field campaign and actual-leachate bench screening be funded immediately, followed by seasonal monitoring and additional wells if the initial conceptual model proves inadequate?
Who will supply treatment-process engineering and operate any selected system, and what space, power, discharge route and residual-waste disposal arrangements are available?
